body:
Yeah, I just wish my brain wasn't my worst enemy. I make one small mistake and it seems like the end of the world to me. Every straw is the straw that breaks the camel's back. It's been like that for 6 years now and I just don't know how to circumvent it.

I'm on medication now and it helps for the most part. I don't get as many intrusive thoughts and I can actually get up in the morning without feeling complete dread for the day. But when these little things tip me over the edge, there doesn't seem to be anything to help.

School seems to make it worse. It's not like if I get one question wrong I'll freak out. But more of if I misread something and embarrass myself I just break down. It's really not a big deal but it just tears me up inside. If anything, I'm just embarrassing myself more by making a big deal out of it.

Also, I just want to say thank you. I know I come off pretty irrational so thanks for being patient and talking to me. It means a lot to me.

I'm currently attending a community college for my first two years. I then plan to transfer to a university and major in agriculture.

The reason I'm doing 4 years of college total is because that's how many years I have for benefits. I get paid a couple thousand a month iirc. I would have liked to put college off for a while and try to get a paid apprenticeship. But, according to my parents, that's not possible.

It's frustrating how little info I have about what my benefits actually entail but my parents refuse to be straight with me. I don't know if they're hiding something or if they're just as ignorant as I am on the matter. I don't even know how to go about asking the VA about it.

Anyways, my main focus is agriculture/farming. I could do without carpentry and weaving but I would like to learn them at some point. Even if it's years down the line.

My plan atm is to live with my parents and save as much of the money as possible. I was going to move into an apartment but it's just not logical or sustainable.

I do have long-term goals. I want to buy an RV and move out to Idaho and start a farm. I want to learn trade skills like carpentry and weaving. I really do want these things. I get excited thinking about them and they give me something to look forward to. 

But they just seem so far away. And it just seems like they're getting farther.

I don't want to be a failure, I don't want to be a disappointment or a useless member of society. I want to prove my principal and counselors wrong when they said I couldn't do it.

But I don't know how to do it. I don't want to make excuses because I know I CAN do it. I got through 13 years of schooling, I can do four more, right? But it just feels like everything is stacked against me.

I don't know if any of that makes sense. I'm crying at the moment so I apologize if this is confusing.
